headline: Cheapest rent and most park land in Ward 10 pair with the city's lowest income.
summary:
South Deering, Hegewisch, East Side, and part of Riverdale form Ward 10 on the Far Southeast Side. Thirty-two wards score higher than Ward 10, putting it 33rd overall. Its composite score comes to 37.43, roughly in the middle of the pack.

Physical space and cost of living are its clearest strengths. Ward 10 has the most park acreage per resident of the fifty wards, the lowest measured rent in Chicago on both a census survey and real-time listing data, and the lightest air-toxics burden citywide on the environmental justice index used here. The weaker numbers involve crowding and cash income rather than pollution or space. Ward 10 has the lowest count of bars, cafes, gyms, and other gathering spots per resident citywide, and its measured household income sits at the bottom of the list. Off-street parking lots are scarce too. Ward 10 reads as a place with room to breathe and comparatively cheap housing, set against thin nightlife options and comparatively low measured income.
reading_the_rankings: Take the No. 1 rank for rent first. Both the census survey and a real-time listing index put Ward 10 at the cheapest in the city, and that part holds up as a real signal. That census figure gets divided across tracts using their area rather than by where renters actually live, so a tract that crosses into a neighboring ward still contributes its full, evenly divided share to Ward 10's number. The bottom-of-the-list rank on household income tells a thinner story. That figure comes from income data covering several wards at once, so a cluster of neighboring wards ends up with close to the same score by construction, not because of anything specific happening inside Ward 10 itself. The last-place rank for gathering spots like bars, cafes, and gyms sits somewhere in between the two. Two points is the entire gap between Ward 10's count and five other wards, so the rank makes this ward look like more of an outlier than the numbers really support.

news.headline: State, City Sue South Side Vegetable Oil Plant Over 'Foul Odors,' Pollution
news.note: The state and city sued Pullman Innovations, a South Deering vegetable oil plant, over odor complaints and air pollution violations at its East 100th Street facility.

news.headline: Altgeld Gardens Community Center Expansion, Including New Gym, Gets Council OK
news.note: City Council approved a $24 million renovation and expansion of the Up-Top Building in Altgeld Gardens, run by youth nonprofit By The Hand Club For Kids.

news.headline: Baby Eagles' Nest Gets Extra Protection As Park District Blocks Far South Side Trail
news.note: The Park District closed a trail near a South Deering nest where two bald eaglets hatched, the first documented successful hatching in the city in more than a century.

news.headline: Dozens Of Decomposing Bodies Found In Southeast Side Funeral Home
news.note: State and city investigators found 57 decomposing bodies at the South Chicago Chapel funeral home in South Deering after a license-violation tip.
